data.claim: Running the base's own test files fails the test when it pre-exists broken; else a ddflow-applied mutation of a changed test file makes it fail
data.falsifier: the new tests passing before the change, or a surviving mutation being accepted
data.mechanism: verify_regression_test overlays only the new test file on the base; a test-file fix rides along in the overlay
data.probe: tests/test_regression_testfix.py: 6 cases (restored files, mutation kills, mutation survives, mutation outside diff, CLI flags, source+test fix still refused)
data.question: Can a fix confined to test files be verified by ddflow?

chunk_findings.detail: If the fix deletes a test file (a legitimate test-file-only change), the loop copies that deletion into the scratch tree via `dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)`. The agent can then name that deleted file as the mutation `file` (it is in `changed`, so the `rel not in changed` guard passes, and `old` need only be non-empty), and `target.read_text("utf-8")` raises `FileNotFoundError`, crashing the close with a traceback instead of returning the intended "mutation cannot be applied" refusal (PASSES). The failure is concrete: fix deletes `tests/test_x.py`; `--mutation-file tests/test_x.py --mutation-old foo --mutation-new bar` → uncaught exception.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py `_by_mutation`

chunk_findings.detail: In the "pre-fix test files restored" branch, only `outcome == "failed"` is handled; any other outcome — including `"unavailable"` (e.g. the pre-fix tree lacks a fixture/conftest introduced by the fix, so pytest cannot run there, or the gate runner is unavailable) — silently falls through to the `PASSES` branch, whose recorded reason asserts "the test also passes with the pre-fix test files restored". That records a false claim in the evidence when the run actually could not execute, conflating "could not run" with "passed". The mutation path (`_by_mutation`) treats `"unavailable"` as UNRUN precisely because it is not a pass, so the asymmetry here mis-records the verdict.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py `verify_test_only_fix`

chunk_findings.detail: When the fix deletes a test file and the agent supplies a mutation naming that file, the copy loop takes the `else: dst.unlink(missing_ok=True)` branch, so `target` does not exist in the scratch tree. The subsequent `target.read_text("utf-8")` then raises `FileNotFoundError`, crashing the gate instead of returning a `(status, evidence)` verdict. Repro: fix deletes `tests/test_x.py` (so it appears in `changed`), and mutation is `{"file": "tests/test_x.py", "old": "...", "new": "..."}` — `rel in changed` passes, `old` is non-empty, the merge tree builds fine, and the read blows up. The same crash occurs if the fix renames the file (with `--no-renames` the old path shows up as a deletion in `changed`). The function's own contract says unapplicable mutations must be refused as PASSES, never crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py:_by_mutation

chunk_findings.detail: `restored` is initialized to the literal string "not run (the test is not in the base's test files)", but this value is also used whenever the restored run simply never executed for another reason — specifically when `command` is empty (no gate command could be derived) the code skips `run_command_gate` entirely and `restored` keeps its initial value. In that case the refusal message claims the test "is not in the base's test files", which is false: the test may well exist in the base tree, the run just wasn't performed. This misleads the user about why verification failed and can send them down the wrong remediation path (e.g. adding the test to the base rather than fixing command discovery). Initialize with a neutral "not run" and set the specific reason only in the branch where the test file is genuinely absent from the base.

chunk_findings.detail: These two tests pin down, as the *desired* behaviour, that a fix-run which never produced a verdict (`"unavailable"`, reason `"timed out after 600s"`) makes `api.bug_fixed(...)` return `out.exit == OK` (`assert out.exit == OK and out.data["regression_verified"] == "could-not-run"` in test 3; `assert out.exit == OK` in test 4). The stated intent of the bug is only that the message must "say why" — the complaint is that `complete --regression-test` reported `(failed)` for a test that actually passes, masking the real verdict. Turning the hard gate into a soft one goes beyond that: with a slow enough machine, the regression run times out on every attempt and each attempt now returns success, so `ddflow complete --regression-test <slow test>` closes the bug even though the regression test never ran, let alone passed. The triggering input is exactly the bug's own environment (load average ~200, test takes >600 s, so `ev["reason"] == "timed out after 600s"`): previously the command refused (noisily, with a wrong verdict), now it reports 0 and the bug is closed with no passing regression test — i.e. the same masking, in the other direction. This conflicts with the recorded precedence rule that ddflow workflow enforcement is a hard constraint and that a change "must have regression test" [D-rules-hierarchy]: a not-run regression test should not satisfy the gate. The fix for the misleading message is to report the real verdict and the reason (as `describe_run` apparently now does) while still refusing, not to let the verification failure mode (`unavailable`/timeout) unlock completion.

Both lists have the same number of entries (9), i.e. the two new regression-verification knobs were pasted over the two existing ones rather than inserted before them. This change is about the regression-test refusal message, so nothing justifies removing `reflect_after_items`/`test_file_globs`. Run the same command whose args are in this array element (the `--explain` invocation) against the fixed tree: if the code still defines those two knobs, its output contains them and the transcript comparison fails on exactly this array element; if the code no longer emits them, the change silently deleted two documented configuration knobs (the lessons refelction counter and the test-file glob list) as a side effect of a bug-fix transcript refresh. Either way the fixture and the code disagree.

chunk_findings.detail: `_NOT_A_TEST_FAILURE = (4, 5)` is documented as "pytest exit codes that mean it ran no test", and by its name it is the exclude-set used to separate *could-not-run* from *the test genuinely failed*. Pytest returns 2 (not 4/5) both when execution is interrupted **and when collection fails** (e.g. `ERROR tests/test_x.py - ImportError`), and 3 for an internal error. Those runs are therefore classified as a real test failure rather than as "could not run". That is exactly the situation this feature creates: the fixed test file is replayed against the pre-fix tree, where a module/helper/fixture it imports may not exist yet, so a collection error is a likely outcome. Concrete input: `ddflow complete fix-Bc262739f62 --regression-test tests/test_review_triage_gate.py::test_x` where the test module imports a helper added by the fix; on the prefix tree pytest exits 2 before collecting anything, the prefix run is read as "the test fails on the prefix" instead of `REGRESSION_COULD_NOT_RUN`, and the gate can report the fix as regression-verified on a run in which no assertion was ever executed. Codes 2 and 3 cannot be produced by a test that ran and failed (that is code 1), so they belong in this set (or the check should be inverted to `rc == 1` means "failed").
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py:_NOT_A_TEST_FAILURE

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch converts a non-executing run into a success. In this file `outcome == "passed"` already returns `PASSES` and the genuine-`failed` path is what the gate is supposed to reject (that is the entire point of the mutation check). The added branch intercepts the case where pytest *did not run a test* (exit `2`/`3`/`4`/`5` — collection error, usage error, internal error, or "no tests collected") and returns `PASSES` unconditionally, while its own reason string admits "a mutation that removes or renames the test does not show it guards the fix". Concretely: a fix whose diff deletes/renames the named test (or a `--regression-test` mutation derived from such a fix) reverts the test file such that pytest collects nothing and exits 5; `rev.get("exit")` is in `_NOT_A_TEST_FAILURE`, so the gate returns `PASSES` and `ddflow complete ... --regression-test <test>` closes the bug even though the regression test never executed and never demonstrated that it guards the fix. The inconclusive result should remain `UNRUN` (or a failure), not be reported as success; as written, any mutation that removes the test is a free pass, weakening the hard "must have regression test" constraint [D-rules-hierarchy].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/regression_testfix.py:214 (new `if outcome == "failed" and rev.get("exit") in _NOT_A_TEST_FAILURE` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: `MUTATION_ORDER` used to name exactly the three parameter names that `mutation_of` reads back out of the api argument dict (`mutation_file`, `mutation_old`, `mutation_new`) — the module docstring still describes the surfaces as "both read back as the one `{file, old, new}` dict the api takes", and the unchanged tail of `mutation_of` (lines reading `a.get("mutation_file") or "", a.get("mutation_old") or ""`) proves those keys must still be present in `a` on the command-line path. The new value `("mutation",)` names only the MCP-only JSON parameter and drops the three CLI flag names, so the read-back list no longer covers the parameters that the CLI actually supplies. Given `ddflow complete fix-Bc262739f62 --regression-test tests/test_review_triage_gate.py --mutation-file tests/test_review_triage_gate.py --mutation-old '<fixture text>' --mutation-new '<fix removed>'`, argparse still accepts the three flags (they remain declared, hence `MUTATION_FLAG_EXEMPT` is needed for the parity test), but they are never collected into the dict handed to `mutation_of`; `a.get("mutation")` is empty, the fallback `if not file and not old: return None` fires, and the command runs as if no mutation was given — the same base-with-test-file verification that passes and refuses, i.e. bug Bc262739f62 is reintroduced on the very command line this feature is documented for, while the flags are still advertised to the user. The tuple needs to retain the three CLI parameter names (e.g. `("mutation", "mutation_file", "mutation_old", "mutation_new")`), not replace them with the single MCP parameter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/mutation_params.py:MUTATION_ORDER

chunk_findings.detail: The one behavioural edit in this hunk attaches a flag exemption to the very command whose entire contract is "write the regression test, watch it FAIL against the unfixed code, then close." `bug fixed` is the command that enforces the mandatory regression-test/verification guard, and it now declares its flags exempt (`flag_exempt=MUTATION_FLAG_EXEMPT`), while the surrounding help was simultaneously weakened (the `regression_tests` help loses "One of the two is required.", the `regression_test` help loses the pointer to the list form, and the description loses "the name of"). Given input such as `ddflow bug fixed Bc262739f62 --regression-test tests/test_review_triage_gate.py::test_x` — a test that already passes on the base because the fix is a fixture in the test file itself — the command's flags are exempted from the enforcement contract instead of gaining the promised "verify against the pre-fix version of the test file (or conftest)" path, so the pre-fix check can be bypassed without `--skip-regression-verify`/`--verify-reason` being recorded. That is exactly the enforcement the change was supposed to keep (just pointed at the pre-fix test file), and it contradicts [D-rules-hierarchy], which states ddflow rules are hard constraints (e.g. "must have regression test"). No code in this hunk introduces any mechanism for verifying against the pre-fix test file; it only adds the exemption plus softer wording.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/records.py:205 — `Command(path=("bug", "fixed"), ...)` with `flag_exempt=MUTATION_FLAG_EXEMPT`
